analysis: MARKET REGIME: SPY in confirmed uptrend (+2.4% vs SMA50, +0.77% 20d slope) — a constructive backdrop, but not a license to chase. PORTFOLIO CAPACITY: With 94% deployment and only $1,110 of remaining headroom, there is effectively zero capacity for a new meaningful position. Adding a $1,100 position would be a rounding error and violate disciplined sizing, so new buys are off the table this cycle regardless of candidate quality. POSITION REVIEW — all five held: (1) A +12.67%: Agilent continues to trend well, thesis intact, hold and trail stop higher; (2) AMP +4.49%: Ameriprise solid, financial services uptrend; (3) LMT +6.15%: Defense outperformer, thesis intact; (4) MCO +3.10%: Moody's grinding higher, hold; (5) TEL -4.70%: TE Connectivity is the book's weak link — currently mixed/sideways basing, -5.9% below SMA200, and our cost basis is $215.07 vs. $204.97 market. However, fundamental thesis remains intact: PEG 0.93, fwd P/E 15.88, rev growth +13.8%, EPS revisions positive +2.1%, and ATR-based stop (entry minus ~2x ATR ~6.5pt) would be near $189-192. TEL has NOT broken thesis or stop — hold but monitor closely; a close below $195 or deteriorating EPS revisions would be the trigger to exit. HISTORICAL PERFORMANCE FLAGS: Profit factor of 0.55 and Sortino of -2.47 are sobering. This confirms the mandate — do not manufacture trades. The three WDAY stop-outs reveal the danger of forcing entries in choppy, extended names. CANDIDATES REVIEWED: Several compelling names exist (KKR PEG 0.59, ADBE fwd P/E 9.57, RDDT 61% rev growth, IT low P/E) but none can be sized properly given current deployment. Even the best setup is worthless at $1,100 exposure. CONCLUSION: Cash conservation and position stewardship IS the alpha this cycle. Hold the book, tighten trailing stops on A (consider moving stop to near breakeven ~$130-132 to lock gains), and wait for capacity to open organically via target hits or stop-outs before adding new exposure.
